backlog.spec: Add a fourth column to base_predict's output: a similarity-weighted kNN regressor on the ECFP Tanimoto matrix. For each test molecule, take the k=10 training neighbours with the highest Tanimoto similarity (use the existing tanimoto(Fb, Fa) matrix) and predict the weighted mean of their targets with weights equal to similarity raised to the power 3. Fall back to the training mean when the top similarity is zero. Include the new column in the stack's oof matrix so that the Ridge meta-learner weighs it alongside the other three members.
backlog.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour regression member

backlog.spec: After meta.predict on the oof matrix, fit sklearn.isotonic.IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds='clip') from the oof stacked predictions to y using only the out-of-fold data. Apply that isotonic map to the test-time stacked prediction before returning. This corrects any monotone bias the linear meta-learner leaves, such as compression at the extremes of logD. Keep the Ridge meta-learner as the first stage, and do not change the base learners.
backlog.title: Isotonic recalibration of the stacked output

backlog.spec: Extend featurize with 1024-bit count atom-pair fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator) and 1024-bit topological-torsion fingerprints. Concatenate them before the descriptor block. Update the descriptor slicing, which currently uses 2*N_BITS, to use a constant N_FP equal to the total fingerprint width.
backlog.title: Add atom-pair and RDKit path fingerprints

backlog.spec: In featurize, use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy (count simulation) instead of binary GetFingerprintAsNumPy for both ECFP and FCFP, so the tree models see substructure counts. Keep the Tanimoto kernel input binary by thresholding Ftr[:, :N_BITS] > 0 before casting, or use the min/max Tanimoto on counts.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan features

backlog.spec: Make no change to train.py at all and run the current script as a job. The incumbent loss of 0.4895 rests on a single run and the noise standard deviation per job is about 0.0042, so several of the recent small-delta rejections were decided against an estimate that itself carries roughly that much uncertainty. A second measurement halves the standard error of the incumbent and makes the accept/reject threshold for subsequent ideas much more reliable. If the two runs disagree by more than about 0.01, treat the incumbent as unconfirmed and prefer future candidates with larger deltas.
backlog.title: Replicate the incumbent to confirm its loss

backlog.spec: At the start of fit_predict, clip train_y to its 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles (computed on the training fold only) before fitting everything. Predictions are not clipped. This reduces the influence of outlier labels on the kernel ridge and the trees.
backlog.title: Winsorise extreme training targets

backlog.spec: The random forest base learner is currently RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=200, max_features=0.3, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) with min_samples_leaf defaulting to 1. Set min_samples_leaf=3 and max_features=0.2 so that leaves are smoother and each tree sees fewer features, which often generalizes better across unseen scaffolds. Also set max_samples=0.8 to add bootstrap-style subsampling diversity. Keep n_estimators=200. This is a one-line change to the constructor in base_predict and does not alter the interface.
backlog.title: More regularized random forest

backlog.spec: Replace the Ridge(positive=True) meta-learner with a non-negative weight vector that sums to 1 and minimises the mean absolute error on the out-of-fold predictions. Use scipy.optimize.minimize with a softmax parametrisation, or SLSQP with bounds and a sum constraint, started from equal weights. Predict with the weighted sum of base_te columns. Include no intercept.
backlog.title: L1-optimal meta-learner

backlog.spec: Add a helper that parses each SMILES, keeps the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), and neutralises charges (rdMolStandardize.Uncharger). Use the cleaned molecule in both featurize and desc_vector (cache key stays the original SMILES). Fall back to the original molecule if cleaning fails. Scaffold groups stay computed from the original SMILES.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and neutralisation before featurising

backlog.spec: Extend the KRR base learner's kernel with an atom-pair fingerprint Tanimoto term. In fit_predict, also compute 1024-bit atom-pair fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=1024), GetFingerprintAsNumPy) for train and test as float64 arrays Atr, Ate (not added to the tree features). Pass them through to base_predict, slicing them like Ftr/Fte. In base_predict, use kernel K = T_ecfp + T_ap + wr*RBF, where T_ap = tanimoto(Aa, Aa) and tanimoto(Ab, Aa) for prediction. Keep the existing grid search over lam and wr. Use the same changes in both the inner CV and the final solve.
backlog.title: Multi-fingerprint kernel for KRR

backlog.spec: Add a helper that converts each SMILES to a canonical form with the largest organic fragment kept: parse with Chem.MolFromSmiles, split with rdkit.Chem.rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser, and neutralise with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Apply this helper once to train_smiles and test_smiles at the top of fit_predict, and use the cleaned SMILES for featurize, desc_vector and the Murcko scaffold groups. Keep the original order and length. Fall back to the input SMILES if parsing fails.
backlog.title: Largest-fragment and salt stripping before featurising

backlog.spec: In base_predict, make the RBF bandwidth tunable: add a gamma multiplier g in (0.5, 1.0, 2.0) applied to the current gamma=1/(2*n_desc). Compute Ra for each g once (3 dense matrices) and extend the inner GroupKFold grid over (lam, wr, g), keeping the 4-fold inner CV. Use the best triple for the final solve and the test kernel. Watch runtime: precompute the kernels outside the loops.
backlog.title: RBF gamma scale grid for kernel ridge

backlog.spec: The KRR hyperparameter grid search runs inside every outer stacking fold plus the final fit, which costs a lot of time. Run the (lam, wr) grid search only once per fit_predict call, on the full training set with the existing GroupKFold(4) over scaffold groups. Pass the chosen (lam, wr) into base_predict as an argument and remove the search from base_predict. Use the saved time to widen the grid to lam in (0.05, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0) and wr in (0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0). Predictions otherwise stay the same.
backlog.title: Cheaper KRR search, reused for final fit

backlog.spec: In base_predict, add a CatBoostRegressor (loss_function='MAE', iterations=800, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, thread_count=8, random_seed=seed, verbose=0) fit on Xa (fingerprints plus descriptors) and append its predictions as a 4th column. Change oof to have 4 columns (np.zeros((len(y), 4))). The positive-ridge meta learner then weights it.
backlog.title: Add CatBoost base learner

backlog.spec: Replace the binary Tanimoto kernel with the count-based MinMax kernel on count Morgan (radius 3) vectors. Widen the lam grid to (0.03,0.1,0.3,1.0) and the wr grid to (0.25,0.5,1,2,4). Check whether the KRR column improves the ensemble.
backlog.title: Larger KRR hyperparameter grid with MinMax kernel

backlog.spec: In lgb_params, set learning_rate=0.02 and add bagging_fraction=0.8, bagging_freq=1, lambda_l2=1.0. Set N_ROUNDS=1200. In base_predict, train the LightGBM model with 3 seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2) and average their predictions into p_lgb. Leave every other part unchanged. If the job approaches the 10-minute limit, use 2 seeds instead.
backlog.title: Stronger LightGBM: slower lr, bagging, seed average

backlog.spec: In the kernel member, replace the ECFP Tanimoto kernel with the mean of Tanimoto kernels on ECFP bits (radius 2) and on count-based Morgan features using the min/max (generalised Tanimoto) kernel. Compute count features with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy at radius 3, 1024 bits, in featurize, stored as an extra array passed through. The kernel is sum_i min(a_i,b_i) / sum_i max(a_i,b_i), computed in chunks to bound memory. Keep the RBF term and the grid search.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge with mixed multi-radius Tanimoto

backlog.spec: Wrap fit_predict's final test-time fit in a bagging loop over scaffold groups. Build the Murcko scaffold group array as now, then for each of five repeats with rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + repeat), sample the unique scaffold groups with replacement, take all rows belonging to the sampled groups as the bag, call base_predict on that bag to predict the test molecules, apply the already-fitted meta-learner weights, and store the result. Return the median of the five resulting prediction vectors. To keep inside the time limit, reduce the inner out-of-fold stacking loop that produces the meta-learner's training matrix from five folds to three. Sampling whole scaffolds rather than rows keeps the resampling aligned with how the harness splits data.
backlog.title: Scaffold-group bagged ensemble of the whole stack

backlog.spec: Inside base_predict, train the LightGBM model once for N_ROUNDS and record its predictions at several checkpoints, for example rounds 300, 400, 500 and 600, using m.predict(Xb, num_iteration=k). Average these snapshot predictions to form p_lgb in place of the single final-round prediction. This adds no extra training cost, only extra predict calls. Keep the learning rate and all other parameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Snapshot averaging of the LightGBM member

backlog.spec: Compute a weight for each training molecule from how common its Murcko scaffold is within the training fold: w_i = 1 / sqrt(count of molecules sharing its scaffold). Normalise the weights to mean 1. Pass them as sample_weight to the random forest fit and as the weight argument to lgb.Dataset in base_predict. Leave the kernel members unweighted, because the Tanimoto solve has no natural weight hook. The aim is to reduce the influence of large scaffold families on the trees.
backlog.title: Scaffold-frequency sample weighting

backlog.spec: Compute the generic Murcko scaffold (MakeScaffoldGeneric) for each molecule. Inside base_predict, for the tree learners only, add one column: the out-of-fold smoothed mean of y for the molecule's generic scaffold. Use smoothing m=5 toward the global mean. For training rows, compute it by leave-one-group-out using the Murcko scaffold groups ga. For test rows, use the full-training statistics. Unseen scaffolds get the global mean. Pass the generic scaffold strings through as an extra argument.
backlog.title: Generic-scaffold target-encoding feature

backlog.spec: Replace the Ridge(alpha=1e-3, positive=True) meta-learner with a non-negative least-absolute-deviation fit. Solve min over w >= 0 of sum |oof @ w - y| using scipy.optimize.linprog, with slack variables for the absolute residuals, and then add an intercept term fixed at zero. Use the L1-optimal weights for the final combination of base_te. Keep the oof matrix and the rest of the stack unchanged. The metric is MAE, so this aligns the meta-learner with the scoring.
backlog.title: L1-optimal non-negative meta-learner

backlog.spec: Reduce the LightGBM learning rate from 0.03 to 0.01 and raise num_boost_round from N_ROUNDS=600 to 1500, which usually gives a smoother L1 fit with the same capacity. Change the constant N_ROUNDS to 1500 and the learning_rate in lgb_params to 0.01. Keep num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=10, feature_fraction=0.2. Check that the job stays under the 10-minute limit; if it does not, use 1000 rounds at learning_rate 0.015 instead.
backlog.title: Lower learning rate with more rounds for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Add one round of self-training at the end of fit_predict. After computing the test predictions in the usual way, form an augmented training set consisting of the real training rows plus the test rows carrying their predicted values as pseudo-labels, with sample weights 1.0 for real rows and 0.3 for pseudo-labelled rows. Refit only the LightGBM and random-forest base learners on this augmented set (pass the weights through sample_weight and LightGBM's weight argument), leaving the kernel member and the meta-learner weights from the first pass unchanged, and recombine with the same meta-learner coefficients to give the final predictions. Guard the whole second pass in a try/except that returns the first-pass predictions on any failure, and keep the extra fit cheap enough that total runtime stays well under ten minutes.
backlog.title: Transductive pseudo-label self-training round

backlog.spec: In base_predict, the descriptor RBF kernel currently uses a fixed gamma = 1.0 / (2 * d) where d is the number of descriptor columns. Replace this with the median heuristic: after z-scoring the descriptor block, draw a subsample of at most 1000 training rows with rng = np.random.default_rng(seed), compute the pairwise squared Euclidean distances within that subsample, take the median of the strictly off-diagonal entries, and set gamma = 1.0 / median_sq_dist. Use that gamma inside rbf() for both the train-train kernel and the test-train kernel. Everything else (the lambda and RBF-weight grid search, the RF and LightGBM members, the Ridge meta-learner) stays exactly as it is. The bandwidth is then matched to the actual scale of the data instead of a dimension-based guess, and the cost is negligible.
backlog.title: Median-heuristic RBF bandwidth in the kernel member

backlog.spec: The kernel-ridge member currently grid-searches lambda in (0.1, 0.5, 2.0) and RBF weight in (0.5, 1.0, 2.0) using one np.linalg.solve per combination per inner fold. Restructure this so that for each RBF weight and each inner GroupKFold(n_splits=4) split, the combined kernel K = Ta[itr,itr] + wr * Ra[itr,itr] is factorised once with np.linalg.eigh giving eigenvalues s and vectors U, and then every lambda is evaluated in closed form as w_in = U @ ((U.T @ (y_tr - mu)) / (s + lam)). Because one eigendecomposition serves all lambdas, widen the grid to lam in (0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0) at roughly the current runtime. Select (lam, wr) by summed absolute validation error as now, then refit on the full training block with np.linalg.solve as before. No other part of the script changes.
backlog.title: Eigendecomposition sweep over a wider kernel-ridge lambda grid

backlog.spec: The stack's meta-learner is a Ridge with positive=True and alpha=1e-3, which minimises squared error even though the harness scores mean absolute error. Replace it with a direct L1 fit: solve min over w >= 0 and intercept b of sum_i |y_i - (b + w . oof_i)| using scipy.optimize.linprog with the standard epigraph formulation (one slack variable per training row, two inequality constraints per row, bounds that keep the weights non-negative and the intercept free, method='highs'). Apply the fitted weights and intercept to the base-learner predictions on the test set. If linprog fails to converge, fall back to the existing Ridge. The number of base columns is three, so the program is small and fast.
backlog.title: Non-negative L1 meta-learner via linear programming

backlog.spec: Simplify the stacking step. Replace meta = Ridge(alpha=1e-3, positive=True).fit(oof, y) with a constrained average: solve for non-negative weights summing to 1 by minimizing mean absolute error on the out-of-fold matrix oof against y, using scipy.optimize.minimize with method='SLSQP' and bounds [0,1], constraint sum(w)=1, starting from equal weights. Predict as base_te @ w. This removes the intercept and the free scale, which may overfit less with a small number of base learners, and matches the MAE objective used by the score. Remove the Ridge import if it is no longer used.
backlog.title: Non-negative averaging instead of positive Ridge meta-learner

backlog.spec: Replace the grid search over lam and wr in base_predict with selection by log marginal likelihood. For each (lam, wr) in a 5x5 grid, take the eigendecomposition of Ta + wr*Ra once per wr. Compute the log marginal likelihood cheaply from the eigenvalues, with the targets centred. Choose the best pair and solve once. This removes the inner CV loops and so is faster. Optionally use the saved time to add more wr values.
backlog.title: Gaussian-process style kernel member with learned noise via marginal likelihood

backlog.spec: In the stack's LightGBM member, train 900 rounds with a learning rate that decays from 0.06 to 0.01 along a cosine curve. Implement it with lgb.reset_parameter(learning_rate=lambda i: ...) passed as a callback. Keep the other parameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Cosine-decayed learning rate for LightGBM

memo: Helped: RDKit 2D descriptors (0.7230 to 0.5902), LightGBM with a cheap inner grid (0.5728), FCFP-style Morgan (0.5585), stacking RF, LightGBM and a Tanimoto kernel learner (0.5357), summed Tanimoto+RBF kernel ridge member (0.5062), then grid-searching its lambda and RBF weight (0.4895, incumbent, only 1 run). Did not help: bit filtering (0.7555), bigger Morgan (0.5880), MLP (0.5719), extra fingerprints/counts (MACCS, atom-pair, BRICS, count FPs 0.5087), ionisable SMARTS, 3D descriptors, density weighting (0.5089), xgboost swap (0.5025), DART (0.4914), label propagation (0.5230), product kernel (0.4895, no change), residual linear model (0.4859, within noise). Heavy inner loops caused timeouts and crashes, so watch the 10-minute limit. Next: replicate the incumbent to confirm 0.4895. Then try a better meta-learner or kernel hyperparameters (RBF gamma). Avoid more feature additions and small tweaks.
